title: Prior art for the collective's O measure: Bedau activity, Channon's component-normalised (re-synchronised) shadow, and the MODES persistence filter; the BFF drift error is the one Channon's method fixes
summary: Places o_measure.py and c30's four O findings among published open-endedness measures. Our cohort statistic is Bedau new activity restricted to a birth window with a shadow-tail threshold. Channon's component-normalised statistics (as summarised and validated by Stout & Spector 2005) re-synchronise the shadow to the real population at every snapshot and evolve it for the same number of generations, which is the published fix for the under-drifting census shadow that manufactured significance in c30's BFF analysis. MODES (Dolson et al. 2019) uses a persistence filter that, by its authors' own account, does not remove neutral drift; c30's BFF result is the shadow-vs-persistence comparison they called for. Proposed next step: a re-synchronised census shadow, analysis only.
